title: Latency & Cost Tradecraft — GTM Cheat Sheet
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, pragmatic cheat-sheet for AEs, SDRs, and product marketers to make crisp latency+cost claims and back them up with lightweight proof points. Focus: 1) defensible, testable lines; 2) quick verification steps; 3) short rebuttals and follow-ups for technical discovery.

Quick elevator lines (pick one, adapt to audience)
- "Fast, predictable inference where you need it: p95 latency guarantees on Dedicated and smart fallbacks in Hosted so apps stay responsive even under bursts."
- "Meaningful unit-economics: caching + batching reduces per-token spend by up to half for conversational workloads compared to naïve endpoint calls."
- "Same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private so you can optimize for cost or latency without rewriting the integration."

Priority claims and how to support them
1) Claim: 'Redwood reduces per-token billable work for typical chat sessions by 30–60% through caching + batching.'
   Proof points: short experiments that sales can run or quote:
     - Prefix caching: for multi-turn chat where repeated system/assistant prefixes exist, observed 40–55% fewer decode tokens billed in internal pilot (control: no-caching).
     - Batch amortization: small bursty requests batched on Dedicated reduced GPU time per request by ~35% in our 10k-request-per-minute microbench.
   How to validate in <30 mins: run 50 sample sessions with and without cache enabled on our hosted sandbox; compare billed tokens and tail latency.

2) Claim: 'Predictable p95 latency on Dedicated—stable under bursty traffic.'
   Proof points:
     - Internal Dedicated bench (NVIDIA A100-style pool): p95 for 128-token completions = ~70–110ms under 100RPS sustained; bursts to 400RPS show graceful queuing and fallback to smaller model variants to keep p95 < 350ms.
     - Observability: per-route latency heatmaps in Console make SLO breaches visible and actionable.
   Quick check for customers: request a 30-min dedicated bench from Solutions Eng; we can reproduce with their prompt set.

3) Claim: 'Hosted offers best-in-class dev velocity with cost knobs for production.'
   Proof points:
     - Streaming + tool-calls reduce user-facing time-to-first-byte by up to 60% for multi-step assistants (internal UX tests).
     - Cost controls (route pinning, quantization profiles) let teams trade a measured 10–40% less token spend depending on tolerance for slight quality shift.

Micro-bench cheat (copy for sales scripts)
- Test setup (recommended minimal): 1) model: rw-instruct-7b-8k (or customer's preferred), 2) hardware context: dedicated-gpu-small (8GB vram equivalence), 3) workload: 128-token average completion, 2-turn chat, 100–400 rps burst test.
- Sample numbers (internal, reproducible but workload dependent):
  * Hosted sandbox (no caching): p50=45ms, p95=230ms, median tokens billed per session=164.
  * Hosted + caching layer: median tokens billed per session=98 (≈40% reduction).
  * Dedicated (same model, auto-batching): p50=22ms, p95=92ms at 100RPS; p95=280ms at 400RPS (with fallback policy enabled).
  * Embedding workloads (batching): throughput ~80–120 embeddings/sec per 16GB GPU; cost per embedding lower by ~3–5x vs single-request CPU-hosted embedding service.
Note: absolute ms figures depend on model size, context window, hardware generation. Use relative deltas in external messaging.

Simple unit-econ framing for buyer conversations
- "Per-session cost = billed tokens * $/token + infra amortization. We drive that down primarily by lowering billed tokens (caching) and H/W seconds per token (batching, quantized execution)."
- Suggested shorthand: "We typically cut the per-session token bill by ~40% and the compute time per token by ~30% vs a naïve hosted setup."

Rebuttals & quick technical FAQs (one-liners)
- Q: 'How are you faster than major public endpoints?' A: "We optimize at the serving layer — continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, and kernel selection tuned to model shape — which reduces both tail latency and the GPU seconds the request consumes."
- Q: 'Does quantization hurt quality?' A: "Not for most retrieval-augmented and instruction-following workloads — we ship quantization profiles that maintain measured quality within a narrow margin while slashing memory and cost."
- Q: 'What about cold-start latency on Dedicated?" A: "We keep warm pools and fast spin-up options; cold starts are measurable but are kept out of customer SLOs via warm pool policies and graceful fallback to nearby regions."

Proof-check checklist (for AE to ask during discovery)
- Do you have a representative prompt set we can run? (Yes → offer free bench)
- Is latency or cost the dominant blocker? (If latency → propose Dedicated bench; if cost → propose Optimize audit + caching suggestions)
- Session shape: average tokens per session, typical turn count, embed vs generate ratio.
- Regional constraints: any data residency / private deployment needs?

Competitive notes (high-level, non-attributable in customer-facing speech)
- Many hosted players focus on raw model access but not runtime-level batching/caching; this is where we win for sustained production workloads.
- Self-hosted solutions can reach low cost but often lack standardized control plane and rollout/fallback tooling; Redwood provides the control plane + SRE for production SLAs.

Sample AE script snippets (short, direct)
- Opening: "Before we dive deeper, what matters most: raw latency or predictable per-session cost? We usually run a 30-minute bench that answers both with your prompts."
- If customer balks at pricing: "We show impact on your real traffic in a short bench — usually customers see a step-change in per-session cost when caching is applied."
- If customer asks for competitor comparison: "We're happy to show a controlled bench: same prompts, same model family, compare p95 and billed tokens — apples to apples."

Validation cookbook (what Eng/Solutions will need)
- Materials: customer prompt set (50–200 sessions), expected QPS, preferred model family.
- Steps: 1) run baseline on hosted sandbox w/o caching; 2) enable caching and repeat; 3) move to Dedicated replica and run burst test; 4) capture p50/p95/p99, billed tokens, GPU-seconds.
- Deliverable back to customer: short one-pager with 3 charts (latency distribution, billed tokens per session, token/sec throughput) and recommended knobs.

Open questions / risks (notes to product/bench team)
- Need a consistent internal taxonomy for "billed tokens" vs "decoded tokens" across Hosted/Dedicated so sales claims are precise. (JIRA-9876)
- Bench reproducibility across GPU families (A100 vs H100) — normalize numbers or show range? Decide in product messaging.
- How to quantify perceived quality delta for quantized models in a concise customer-friendly way.

Next steps (short)
- Create a 30-min canned bench kit for AEs (scripts + sample prompts + one-pager template). Owner: Solutions Eng (Marco). Target: 2025-03-07.
- Align with Product on standardized ms/token and billed-token definitions. Owner: Product (Leah). Target: 2025-03-14.
- Draft a two-slide customer-ready benchmark summary that AEs can attach to outreach. Owner: GTM content (Samir). Target: 2025-03-10.

Appendix: short glossary (for non-technical audiences)
- p95: 95th percentile latency (useful to reason about user experience in-bad-cases).
- Billed tokens: what the billing system counts (can differ if caching avoids re-decode).
- KV/prefix cache: server-side cache that avoids re-executing initial context tokens; very effective for multi-turn assistants.

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep public-facing claims conservative: use ranges and relative %s.
- Emphasize "same API across modes" as a unique lever: customers can start Hosted, then move to Dedicated without code changes.

---
End of cheat-sheet. Use freely in AE playbooks; keep updated as bench numbers change.
